idea_units.text: A question is raised about whether to use their own dataset for evaluation, noting that the last five meetings contain clear examples of method changes.
idea_units.uncertainty_note: This is the start of a brainstorming session on evaluation.

idea_units.text: A demo idea is proposed: show that the agent, with its evolving memory, won't retrieve an old, irrelevant topic, whereas a standard language model might. This demonstrates the concept of memory "fading out" based on importance.
The team discusses whether to create a new dataset or use their existing one. An alternative is to synthetically generate a conversation to perfectly illustrate the desired long-term memory scenario.
idea_units.uncertainty_note: The team is exploring options for the demo dataset and has not made a decision.

idea_units.text: The team agrees that their meeting history contains rejected ideas suitable for a demo, but a concern is raised that using only the last five meetings may not be sufficient to demonstrate a long-term memory effect.
idea_units.uncertainty_note: This highlights an unresolved tension between data availability and demo requirements.

idea_units.text: A suggestion to use much older data (e.g., from 20 meetings ago) is countered by the practical constraint that they may not have that much recorded history.
idea_units.uncertainty_note: This points to a potential data availability issue for the long-term memory demo.

idea_units.text: The proposed demo for the May exhibition would have two parts: 1) showing the difference in output compared to a standard RAG model on a historical topic, and 2) demonstrating the "packing" of idea units.
A potential objection to the system is anticipated: it might forget important information that was mentioned a long time ago.

The system's defense against forgetting is that memory retrieval is based on current relevancy during an interaction, and memory importance is updated post-interaction. An old topic, if revisited, will have its importance boosted for the future even if it was temporarily "forgotten".
The memory system has a mechanism where if a memory's importance score is high enough, it will never fade out.
